Apple today released iOS 27.2 beta 1, skipping 27.1 entirely in the testing cycle. The new iOS 27.2 update includes, among other changes, the previously announced all-new Health app.

The all-new Apple Health app debuts in iOS 27.2 beta 1

At last week's September event, Apple unveiled a brand-new Health app coming to iPhone later this year.

Today, beta testers can now get an early look at the revamped Health app with iOS 27.2 beta 1.

When introducing the new Health app, Apple placed special emphasis on how it will use Apple Intelligence to help users better understand their health. Here's how they put it:

Now in iOS 27.2 beta 1, if you're a developer, both the new "Insights" tab and "Longevity" tab are available to try.

Since the new Health app relies on Apple Intelligence, you'll need an AI-capable iPhone to try it out. Some features also require a paired Apple Watch, and your device must be set to English (US).

So if your iPhone is below the iPhone 15 Pro specs, or you don't have a compatible Apple Watch, you won't be able to use the new Health app features. But for everyone else, iOS 27.2 offers a first look at Apple's expanded vision for the Health app.

Note: Apple says more Health features will roll out in subsequent beta releases, such as booking lab work through Quest and personalised recommendations, among others. Also, while the new Health app is already available in beta, Apple says it won't launch with the final release of iOS 27.2 — instead, it'll arrive later this year.

What do you think of the changes to the Health app in iOS 27.2? Drop your thoughts in the comments below.
